control.purpose: The 1px edge of what a hand can use (query bar, range segments, buttons, fields, chips, facet boxes): 3:1 against its surface.

title.purpose: Console. The page heading; 1.375rem on an incident head.

lead.purpose: Console. The first statement of a section.

conclusion.purpose: Console. The incident's conclusion under its stage strip, at most 72ch.

section.purpose: Console. The heading of a panel.

small.purpose: Console. Table cells, facets, range segments, secondary lines, notes.

badge.purpose: Console. Badges, the severity word, the top bar's stage modes.

label.purpose: Console. Uppercase: column heads, table group rows, facet and rail group titles, stage names, stat labels.

figure.purpose: Console. The monospace number of a stat tile.

mono.purpose: Console. The query, ids, payloads, catalog actions.

mono-cell.purpose: Console. Ids, times, durations and costs in a table row.

site-display.purpose: Site. The one headline of the first screen.

site-headline.purpose: Site. The heading of a band, and the closing question.

site-rule.purpose: Site. A flight rule, stated as a heading.

site-answer.purpose: Site. The level named by the dial, and the last Go key.

site-count.purpose: Site. The T-5 to T-0 numerals of the countdown.

site-title.purpose: Site. A station in the poll, a sub-heading under the dial, the board's clock.

site-station.purpose: Site. A row's name on a board, a countdown step, the Go and No-go keys, the wordmark.

site-key.purpose: Site. The dial's keys, the guard's cover, a video title in the reel.

site-button.purpose: Site. The two buttons of the hero.

site-lamp.purpose: Site. The word in a lamp, a monitor tab.

site-nav.purpose: Site. The top strip's links and a board's heading line.

site-nav-compact.purpose: Site. The top strip's links under 60rem.

site-tag.purpose: Site. Voice tags and the Copy key.

site-lede.purpose: Site. The paragraph under the headline.

site-body.purpose: Site. Running text, at most 46rem wide.

site-note.purpose: Site. A finding on a board row, fine print, the footer.

site-caption.purpose: Site. A figure caption or a tip.

site-code-name.purpose: Site. An action's name in the catalog.

docs-display.purpose: Docs. The page title, at MkDocs Material's root size.

docs-headline.purpose: Docs. A section heading, under a 2px rule.

docs-label.purpose: Docs. Tabs, table heads, admonition titles.

colorSchemes.console: Each custom property is one light-dark(light, dark) value. Frontmatter keys ending in -dark are the dark value of the same variable. The scheme follows the system unless data-theme is set on <html> by the switch in the top bar.
colorSchemes.site: Dark only (color-scheme: dark). The documentation also has MkDocs Material's light scheme, where links use docs-link-light and docs-accent-light.

shadows.name: console-pop
shadows.purpose: --shadow-pop: the phone's More menu, the one element that floats. Panels have none (--shadow: none).

shadows.name: console-live-ring
shadows.purpose: A flat 3px ring around the live dot (--crit-bg when stale). A stroke, not elevation.

motion.name: console-state-ease
motion.purpose: Hover, border and background changes on buttons, checks, pick rows.

motion.name: console-refresh-interval
motion.purpose: The explorer refetches itself with its filters; paused while hidden or under focus. A changed row is tinted and tagged, not moved.

motion.name: site-ease
motion.purpose: The one easing curve (--ease): a row coming up, the guard's cover.

motion.name: site-state
motion.purpose: Fill, text and border colour of lamps, buttons, keys, tabs.

motion.name: site-row-reveal
motion.purpose: A board row coming up from 38% opacity when its station is called.

motion.name: site-poll-step
motion.purpose: The poll, called row by row from script.

motion.name: site-guard-hinge
motion.value: transform 500ms, opacity 350ms; perspective(40rem) rotateX(-96deg) from the top edge

motion.name: site-hold-blink
motion.purpose: The HOLD lamp of the YOU row. The only thing that repeats.

motion.name: site-executor-steps
motion.value: Apply at 1300ms, Verify at 2900ms, done at 4700ms after Go
motion.purpose: The executor's row after an answer.

motion.name: reduced-motion
motion.purpose: No animation, no transition, no smooth scroll; the site's poll is shown complete.

breakpoints.name: console-rows
breakpoints.purpose: Secondary table columns, record rows on a grid, findings in two columns, pick rows in three columns.

breakpoints.name: console-strip
breakpoints.purpose: The incident's stage strip as five columns.

breakpoints.name: console-desk
breakpoints.purpose: The 13rem rail, gutter 1.5rem, the explorer as a table with sticky heads, facets beside it; the tab bar goes.

breakpoints.name: console-side
breakpoints.purpose: The incident page's 18rem sticky side column.

breakpoints.name: site-rows
breakpoints.purpose: Board rows on one line; the dial's keys in one row of four.

breakpoints.name: site-pairs
breakpoints.purpose: Dial text beside the phone; countdown numeral beside its step.

breakpoints.name: site-band-head
breakpoints.purpose: Band head in 5 and 7 columns, station columns, the full navigation.

breakpoints.name: site-hero
breakpoints.purpose: The two-column first screen; the reel beside the video.

stripes.name: site-blanked-hatch
stripes.purpose: The catalog position that does not exist.

delivery.console: Nothing is loaded from another host and there is no inline style (the postmortem page alone allows it for its bundled diagram library): system fonts, one stylesheet, small scripts (theme, console, diagrams), inline SVG icons. Chart, meter and track sizes are SVG attributes or classes.
delivery.site: Barlow Condensed (500, 600, 700), Barlow (400, 500, 600) and JetBrains Mono (400, 600) are loaded from the Google Fonts stylesheet by website/index.html and mkdocs.yml. One stylesheet and one script for the landing page; videos are drawn on a canvas by website/videos/kit.js.

narrative.overview:
Paeon has two visual worlds. They are separate on purpose, and a surface belongs to exactly one.

In the frontmatter, a token with no prefix belongs to the console. A token that starts with `site-` belongs to the site, and one that starts with `docs-` exists only in the documentation theme. Nothing crosses: the console never takes a `site-` token, and the site never takes a console token. The two worlds share one idea and nothing else: what a model said is violet. The site's model violet is the same value as the console's dark-scheme one.

Every section below has a **Console** part and a **Site** part.

The console is an observability tool, in the family its operator already works in (Datadog, OpenObserve). Every list that grows is a dense table, paged by the server, under a query bar and a time range, with status tabs that carry counts and facets that narrow it. Every incident page leads with its stage outcomes and its conclusion, and the evidence follows. It is quiet and flat: cool neutral ground, white or near-black panels, 1px hairlines, one blue accent, and colour kept for state.

It replaced, in turn, the "Strip Bay" console and a generic card-per-incident app. Three things carried over, because they come from the product and not from a look:

The site is a launch-day status board. Each station of Paeon reports in turn on a deep navy ground, in chalk-white condensed capitals, and answers with a lit cell: green GO, amber HOLD, red NO-GO. The last row holds on YOU, beside a striped guard over the one switch that acts. The board is the argument of the page: a visitor sees where thinking stops and doing starts because the poll stops there.

The page is dark only (`color-scheme: dark`), flat, ruled and square. It has no card grid, no shadow and no soft gradient. What reads as a sentence is set in Barlow in sentence case; what reads as a label, a station or an answer is set in Barlow Condensed capitals.

The documentation wears the same board at reading size: condensed capital headings, amber links, square code blocks and tables, with a plain Barlow body. It also has a light scheme (MkDocs Material's white page under the navy header), where amber darkens to stay readable. The three videos are drawn on a canvas from the same palette, copied by value into `kit.js`.
keyCharacteristics: A navy board in four tonal steps, with hairline rules between rows.
Status is a lit square cell with its word inside: GO, HOLD, NO-GO.
Barlow Condensed capitals for stations, headings and keys; Barlow for sentences; JetBrains Mono for commands and catalog names.
Square corners everywhere, and no shadow.
One guarded switch: lift the hazard-striped cover, then press.
Every example is fictional and says so on the board (`Simulated`) and in the footer.
Console: Dense tables: 2.25rem rows, sticky small-capital column heads, monospace for ids, times, durations and costs.
Console: A query bar with a time range, status tabs with counts, facets beside the table.
Console: A five-square stage track on every incident row, and a stage strip on the incident page.
Console: 6px corners on panels, 4px on buttons and fields, pills only for badges and counts.
Console: No shadow on any panel; one floating menu casts the only shadow.

rules.name: The Stage Track Rule
rules.body: Five squares, always in the order triage, investigation, plan, action, postmortem: violet filled when a model answered, green filled when code did it, red filled when it failed, a blue outline on the info tint when it waits, empty when skipped, a dashed hairline when the stage is off. Each square carries its stage and outcome as a title and the track as an image label, and the explorer prints the legend under the table.

rules.name: The Model Voice Rule
rules.body: Violet is the colour of a model's words and of a model-answered stage, and nothing else. The tokens, cost, duration and failure of a model call are ink.

rules.name: The Counted Is Mono Rule
rules.body: A value a person compares down a column (an id, a time, a duration, a cost, a count) is monospace. A sentence never is.

rules.name: The Label Names Data Rule
rules.body: Uppercase belongs to labels that name a column, a group, a facet, a stage or a figure. It never stands above a heading as a teaser.

rules.name: The Flat Panel Rule
rules.body: No panel, row or card casts a shadow. Only a menu that floats over the page takes `--shadow-pop`.

rules.name: The Lamp Rule
rules.body: A status colour is a lit cell with its word in it. Green is GO, amber is HOLD, red is NO-GO; the cell is filled, its text is Deep Navy, and the word is always there. An unlit cell is a Rule Blue outline with Faint Chalk text. A cell at work (`Apply`, `Verify`) is an amber outline with amber text.

rules.name: The Violet Is A Voice Rule
rules.body: Violet marks words a model produced, on the site as in the console, and a `Model` tag stands beside them. It is never an accent.

rules.name: The Ink On Light Rule
rules.body: Text on amber, green, red, violet or Chalk is Deep Navy. Chalk text never sits on a lit colour.

rules.name: The Capitals Rule
rules.body: Capitals belong to Barlow Condensed, and to things that are one line: a heading, a station, a key, a tag. Anything read as a sentence is Barlow in sentence case. The heading line of a board (the incident's name) stays condensed but in its own case.

rules.name: The Tracking Rule
rules.body: The smaller the capitals, the wider the tracking: 0.01em on the display, 0.06em to 0.1em on titles and stations, 0.12em to 0.16em on lamps, keys and tags.

rules.name: The Ruled Row Rule
rules.body: A list starts under a 2px Chalk rule, and each row ends on a 1px Rule Blue hairline. Rows are not boxed, not shaded in turn and not laid out as a grid of cards.

rules.name: The No Shadow Rule
rules.body: Nothing on the site casts a shadow or glows. A lamp is lit by its fill, not by a halo.

rules.name: The Square Rule
rules.body: No radius on the site, the docs or the video player. The one exception is a picture of another device: the phone and its notification keep a phone's round corners (`site-pictured-phone`, `site-pictured-notification`, `site-pictured-notification-key`), on the page and in the videos. Those three values are for that picture only.

rules.name: The Hard Stripe Rule
rules.body: Stripes have hard stops and mean "guarded" or "blanked". A gradient that fades from one colour to another is not used anywhere.

rules.name: The Two Step Rule
rules.body: The control that acts is under a guard: lift, then press. Nothing else on the site takes two steps, and nothing that acts takes one.

dos: Console: **Do** put a growing list in a server-paged table under a query bar, a range and status tabs, with its filters in the URL.
Console: **Do** put the five-square stage track on an incident row, in its fixed order.
Console: **Do** mark every word a model produced: violet, with a Model badge or a model tag nearby.
Console: **Do** write severity and state as a word beside or inside its colour.
Console: **Do** set ids, times, durations, costs and counts in monospace.
Console: **Do** say what was not done in a note: a stage that is off, a failed call, a spent budget.
Console: **Do** define a new colour as one `light-dark()` token and check both schemes.
Console: **Do** give a control the `control` edge and keep targets at 2.5rem for buttons and fields.
Site: **Do** put a status in a lamp, with its word: GO, HOLD, NO-GO, or the fact itself (`In catalog`, `Proposed`, `Blanked`).
Site: **Do** set text on a lit colour in Deep Navy.
Site: **Do** lay new content out as ruled rows under a 2px Chalk rule.
Site: **Do** keep violet for a model's words and put a `Model` tag beside them.
Site: **Do** mark a simulated incident as simulated on the board that shows it.
Site: **Do** keep sentences in Barlow, sentence case, at 46rem wide at most.
donts: Console: **Don't** load a font, script, image or style from another host, or write a `style` attribute.
Console: **Don't** list incidents as a stack of cards, or let a page grow without paging.
Console: **Don't** put a shadow on a panel, row or card; `--shadow-pop` is for the floating menu.
Console: **Don't** use a state colour for decoration, or violet for something code recorded.
Console: **Don't** add a control that approves or runs anything beyond Go on a waiting plan, which the executor itself allows; nothing set in the console configures what acts.
Console: **Don't** print a stored secret back into a page, or put a second filled button in a form.
Site: **Don't** round a corner, except on the picture of the phone.
Site: **Don't** add a shadow, a glow or a gradient that fades. Hard stripes belong to the guard and to the blanked position.
Site: **Don't** use green, amber or red for anything but go, hold and no-go, and what you can press.
Site: **Don't** set a sentence in capitals, or Barlow Condensed in a paragraph.
Site: **Don't** bring a console token, a pill badge or a rounded card onto the site, or a `site-` token into the console.
Site: **Don't** put a second solid amber button on a screen.
